1	# Handoff — Make nv.ollama-code-mcp.ai safe for Protect mode (WAF sensors bound & validated)
2	Written: 2026-07-31 00:45 · Session: ~30 turns
3	
4	> Supersedes the PR-#38 handoff. Everything it queued is done except the ticket
5	> board (user deprioritized it). Context: user has a **job technical screening
6	> today** and this cluster is the demo environment — bias toward not breaking it.
7	
8	## Where things stand
9	
10	All prior work is closed: neuvector-mcp **1.0.3** is built (in-cluster BuildKit
11	→ `registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/neuvector-mcp:1.0.3`, digest `27a38dc89bd6…`),
12	deployed, and the workload-projection fix **verified end-to-end over MCP**.
13	PRs #38 and #39 are merged; local `main` may be one merge behind — fetch first.
14	
15	`/fossa-protect` ran against `ollama-code-mcp` to completion for the first time,
16	including live paired-probe validation. Two sensors exist and are **bound to
17	`nv.ollama-code-mcp.ai` with action=deny**; the group is in **Discover**, so
18	they alert only.
19	
20	**NEW TASK (not started):** implement appropriate rules so
21	`nv.ollama-code-mcp.ai` can be moved to **Protect** mode and the service still
22	functions. Protect enforces three things at once: network policy (whitelist),
23	process/file profiles, and the WAF deny bindings become real blocking.
24	
25	## The target deployment (facts gathered this session)
26	
27	- Pod `ollama-code-mcp-…` in ns `ai`, service `ollama-code-mcp.ai`, group
28	  `nv.ollama-code-mcp.ai` (learned, Discover, 2 members, 4 policy rules —
29	  rules themselves not yet reviewed).
30	- Transport: **streamable-http only**, port 8765, **no auth configured**.
31	- Ingress paths: traefik ingress `mcp-ollama.ash4d.com` path `/mcp`,
32	  LoadBalancer `192.168.7.165:8765`, clusterIP `10.43.55.56`, service DNS forms,
33	  pod CIDR `10.42.x.x`. Probes are `tcpSocket` (never reach the WAF).
34	- Egress: `ollama-exporter.ai.svc.cluster.local:9401` (OLLAMA_BASE_URL) + DNS.
35	- Running image `ghcr.io/darthzen/ollama-code-mcp:latest` has **mcp 1.28.1**
36	  (all 5 FOSSA mcp CVEs patched as-deployed; repo manifest still pins 1.6.0 —
37	  the recommended dev-side fix, deliberately not done here).
38	
39	## WAF state (created + validated this session)
40	
41	- `sensor.ollama-code-mcp-rebind` — rule.host-not-allowed +
42	  rule.origin-not-allowed, two-pattern `regex`+`!regex` allowlist shape over
43	  the ingress set above.
44	- `sensor.ollama-code-mcp-canary` — rule.ws-upgrade-canary +
45	  rule.bad-session-id (`!regex` on `[0-9a-f]{32}`).
46	- Paired probes from this Mac via the LB: clean → **0 events**; foreign
47	  Host/Origin, `Upgrade: websocket`, malformed `Mcp-Session-Id` → each fired
48	  its exact rule. `context:"header"` **matches header names** (enforcer
49	  v5.6.0) — the skill reference was updated from UNVERIFIED to verified.
50	
51	## What Protect-readiness still requires (why this is not just a mode flip)
52	
53	1. **rule.bad-session-id was never probed with a VALID session id.** Only the
54	   malformed case (fires) and no-session-id case (silent) are proven. If the
55	   SDK's real session-id format is not exactly 32 lowercase hex, this rule
56	   blocks every legitimate session in Protect. Drive a real MCP
57	   initialize→session flow and confirm zero events before Protect. If the
58	   format can't be confirmed, drop the rule or rebind it action=allow.
59	2. **Origin allowlist vs real clients.** Clean probe sent no Origin. A client
60	   that sends any unlisted Origin (Claude Desktop? browser-based inspectors?)
61	   would be blocked. Watch Discover-mode events over real usage first — the
62	   current binding is a free dry run: any event now = a block under Protect.
63	3. **Network policy**: review the group's 4 learned rules
64	   (`nv_get_network_rule`/`nv_list_network_rules`) against the enumerated
65	   ingress/egress; LB traffic arrives SNAT'd as `Workload:ingress` from
66	   10.42.0.1. Missing learned rules → Protect drops real traffic.
67	4. **Process profile** (`nv_get_process_profile("nv.ollama-code-mcp.ai")`):
68	   never looked at. `kubectl exec` sessions (used this session to check the
69	   mcp version!) will violate it — don't exec into the pod after Protect.
70	5. Mode change itself: `nv_set_group_policy_mode` — deliberately NOT
71	   allowlisted; it will prompt. Two-step confirm handshake like all writes.
72	   Consider Monitor as the staging step; skill notes Discover/Monitor are
73	   equivalent for WAF, but Monitor stops new network-rule learning.
74	
75	## Decisions made (and why)
76	
77	- **Sensors are real mitigations, not stopgaps** — user was explicit: the
78	  security team must be able to act without waiting on dev teams that may
79	  never patch. Framing encoded in the skill and in memory
80	  (`waf-mitigations-are-real`). Don't re-litigate; don't undersell.
81	- Canary + rebind sensors kept `action=deny` in Discover intentionally —
82	  Protect-mode blocking is now the *goal*, not a hazard, but only after the
83	  validations above.
84	- Threat-event queries **must use `side="server"`** — default client-side
85	  filtering returns 0 events for inbound attacks (client is
86	  `Workload:ingress`, empty namespace). Hit live; now in the skill.
87	- WAF sensor `comment` ≤ 256 chars — `len()` it before the first handshake;
88	  the plan step does not pre-validate (hit live again this session).
89	
90	## Files touched
91	
92	- `~/.claude/skills/fossa-protect/SKILL.md` — new "why this exists" framing;
93	  `side="server"` mandatory in step 7; comment-cap hardened; exec-based
94	  artifact correlation + "running artifact newer than findings" section.
95	- `~/.claude/skills/fossa-protect/references/waf-wire-contract.md` —
96	  header-context section now VERIFIED (v5.6.0) with probe evidence; threat
97	  event shape + side="server" trap documented.
98	- Repo: version bump to 1.0.3 everywhere (merged via PR #39). Working tree
99	  clean; branch checked out at end of session: `chore/bump-1.0.3` (safe to
100	  delete after confirming merge; switch to `main` and pull).
101	- Memory: `waf-mitigations-are-real.md` + `MEMORY.md` index created.
102	
103	## What's verified vs assumed
104	
105	**Verified:** 1.0.3 pod runs pushed digest and `nv_list_workloads` /
106	`nv_get_workload` return fully populated fields over MCP against it. Both
107	sensors round-trip exactly; binding live; paired probes behaved as designed;
108	group still Discover. Enforcer v5.6.0 connected on sdf1.
109	
110	**Assumed / NOT established:** valid-session-id traffic is clean (see above);
111	real-client Origin behavior; learned network rules' completeness; process
112	profile contents; whether `(?i)` flags and regex semantics hold in Protect
113	(blocking) path identically to alerting path — no reason to doubt, never
114	tested.
115	
116	## Next step
117	
118	Review the group's learned network rules and process profile, then drive a
119	real MCP session through the LB and watch
120	`nv_query_security_events(kind="threat", side="server", namespace="ai")` for
121	false positives. Only after zero-FP evidence: fix/add rules as needed, then
122	`nv_set_group_policy_mode` → Protect (prompts; two-step confirm) and re-run
123	the paired probes expecting the attack probe to be **denied**, clean to pass.
124	
125	## Open questions
126	
127	- Keep rule.bad-session-id under Protect, or downgrade/drop it if the valid
128	  format can't be confirmed quickly?
129	- Should the no-auth posture itself be fixed (bearer tokens supported by the
130	  chart?) rather than compensated — or is unauthenticated-but-Protected the
131	  intended demo story for the screening?
132	- Permission classifier flakiness: allowlisted `nv_*` tools were sporadically
133	  denied this session; user approval via `/permissions` cleared it. If it
134	  recurs, stop and hand back rather than retry-looping.
135	
136	## Carried forward (unchanged from previous handoff)
137	
138	1. `lab-memory` WAF sensors never created; re-run `/fossa-protect` fresh.
139	2. `ollama-code-mcp` repo needs `mcp>=1.28.1` + `pytest>=9.0.3` manifest bump
140	   (separate repo, deliberately untouched). `lab-memory` needs same mcp bump.
141	3. Ticket board `agent-tools.py doctor --fix` review (user deprioritized).
142	4. `config._env("")` xfail; E501 ignore; iam_read/iam_write fold — cosmetic.
143	5. Do NOT add neuvector-mcp to Fleet until user says so.
144	6. WAF writes stay in `policy_write` toolset — settled.

  secret-key: REPLACE_ME

The fix is done and green — full suite passes, ruff and mypy clean. Here's where things stand.

## What happened

**The flip to Protect silently failed — and it's a bug in neuvector-mcp itself.** `nv_set_group_policy_mode` PATCHes `/v1/group/{name}` with a `policy_mode` field, but the project's own spec (`RESTGroupConfig`, Appendix B) shows that object has no such field — the controller answers 200 and drops it. Policy mode actually lives on the **service**, set via `PATCH /v1/service/config`. That's why the tool reported "applied" while the group stayed in Discover, and why the post-flip attack probes came back `action: alert` instead of deny.

**I've fixed the code** (`src/neuvector_mcp/tools/policy_write.py`): the tool now derives the service name (`nv.X.ns` → `X.ns`), calls `PATCH /v1/service/config`, and rejects custom groups with a clear error since only learned groups carry a mode. Tests updated to the new wire shape plus a new rejection test — all passing, uncommitted on `main` awaiting your review. The deployed 1.0.3 server still has the bug, so the MCP tool can't flip the mode until an image rebuild.

**Good news along the way:** the Protect-readiness validation is fully done, and better than expected:
- Real MCP sessions through both the LB and the traefik ingress completed cleanly with **zero WAF events**, and the session-id format is confirmed 32-lowercase-hex (twice) — `rule.bad-session-id` is safe at deny.
- Driving the traefik path in Discover learned the missing rule **10259** (`nv.traefik.kube-system → group`), closing the one network gap I found. Zero violations anywhere.
- The full threat log shows only the 4 deliberate probe events — no false positives in ~7h of deny-bound Discover.

# Handoff

Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue this work, so the current
session can be ended without losing ground.

**Why this exists.** Every turn re-reads the entire accumulated prefix, so cost
per turn climbs with session length — measured at ~26K cache-read tokens per
turn in short sessions versus ~109K past 100 turns. Ending a long session at a
clean boundary and restarting with a handoff is the largest available
efficiency lever. The handoff is what makes ending cheap.

## Where to write it

```
~/.claude/handoffs/<cwd-with-slashes-as-dashes>.md
```

For example, `/Users/rashford/Developer/kitsune` →
`~/.claude/handoffs/-Users-rashford-Developer-kitsune.md`

Overwrite any existing file for this directory — the newest handoff wins. The
`SessionStart` hook loads it automatically in the next session, so **do not**
paste the contents back into chat.

## What to write

Aim for something a competent stranger could act on. Be concrete: real paths,
real command names, real decisions. Skip anything reconstructible from the repo
or from `git log` — those are already available to the next session.

```markdown
# Handoff — <one-line description of the work>
Written: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · Session: <turns> turns

## Where things stand
Two or three sentences. What was being worked on and what state it is in
right now — not a history of the session.

## Decisions made (and why)
Only decisions that would otherwise be re-litigated. Include the reasoning,
because the reasoning is the part that gets lost.

## Files touched
- `path/to/file` — what changed and why

## What's verified vs assumed
Explicit. If tests ran, say so and give the result. If something was assumed
and never checked, say that too — this is the section that prevents the next
session from building on sand.

## Next step
The single next action, stated concretely. Then anything queued behind it.

## Open questions
Things the user needs to decide, or that were left unresolved.
```

## Procedure

1. **Write the file.** Use the path convention above. Do not ask where to put it.
2. **Confirm briefly** — one line naming the file and the next step it records.
3. **Tell the user to `/clear`** (or start a new session). Do not run `/clear`
   yourself; it is theirs to trigger.

## Notes

- Leave out anything sensitive — the handoff is plain text on disk.
- Handoffs older than 14 days are ignored by the loader.
- To skip loading a handoff for one session, start with `HANDOFF_DISABLE=1`.
- If the user asks for a handoff without wanting to stop, write it anyway and
  skip the `/clear` suggestion.
